entries.title: Undergraduate Research Assistant, Pulsed Laser Template Engineering (PLATEN)
entries.org: Center for Quantum Research and Technology (CQRT), University of Oklahoma
entries.body: I started in the cleanroom, using photolithography, reactive ion etching and pulsed laser deposition to build and test high-aspect-ratio micro- and nanostructures. Most of my time went into tuning the plasma etch (gas chemistry, RF power and chamber pressure) to get vertical sidewalls and a controlled feature depth. I also grew LAO on STO by pulsed laser deposition, watching the growth with RHEED. Now I'm starting on the design side in the same group, on optically bistable ring resonators.
entries.mediaAlt: Sample wafer after photolithography and plasma etching in the cleanroom.

entries.title: Electrical Systems Member
entries.body: I'm designing the Hub board for our IGVC 2027 robot in Altium: a 4-layer PCB that takes power from the battery and sends 12 V power, the CAN bus and the hardware E-Stop line to seven boards, with a current sensor on every port. I chose the reverse-polarity protection, the 3.3 V buck converter and the microcontroller, and I'm now laying out the board. Before that, I planned the robot's component placement and wire routing in Onshape.

entries.title: Peer Learning Assistant
entries.org: Student Learning Center, University of Oklahoma
entries.body: I mentor 250+ students every semester in Physics I and II, Calculus I to III and General Chemistry I. Most of the job is explaining the same idea in a few different ways until it clicks, and breaking a problem into steps students can repeat on their own.

entries.title: Research Apprentice, Light–Matter Interaction (Dr. Tischler)
entries.org: Center for Quantum Research and Technology (CQRT), University of Oklahoma
entries.body: I reviewed research papers on quantum optical effects in silicon carbide and other wide-bandgap semiconductor nanocrystals, and learned how the lab's optical spectroscopy setups measure them. This is where I first got interested in photonics.

entries.title: Research Apprentice, Cloud Microphysics (Dr. McFarquhar)
entries.org: National Weather Center, University of Oklahoma
entries.body: I analyzed aircraft data from the CAESAR campaign, where an NSF/NCAR C-130 flew through cold-air outbreaks out of Kiruna, Sweden. My question was how cloud properties change with altitude, so I compared water content, particle size and condensation-nuclei concentration from several probes against normalized cloud height. I did all the data processing and plots in Python (NumPy, Pandas, Matplotlib).
entries.mediaAlt: Research poster on Arctic cloud microphysics from the CAESAR campaign
